key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Sudden, preceded by prodrome (warning signs). LOCATION: Generalized, loss of consciousness. DURATION: Seconds to 1-2 minutes, brief. CHARACTER: Lightheadedness, tunnel vision, nausea, sweating before fainting. AGGRAVATING: Prolonged standing, heat, dehydration, pain, emotional stress, sight of blood. RELIEVING: Lying down, recovery rapid once horizontal. TIMING: Single episode or rare episodes with clear triggers. SEVERITY: Complete LOC but brief. KEY POSITIVES: Prodrome (warning), rapid recovery, no confusion post-event, clear trigger, young patient. KEY NEGATIVES: NO exertional syncope (cardiac), NO chest pain, NO palpitations before event, NO seizure activity.

red_flags: Chest pain or palpitations before syncope
Family history of sudden cardiac death
